subject: Firefly - executive command lane: throughput spike and recovery plan
messages:
From: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@firefly.ai>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: dana.liu@firefly.ai, procurement@firefly.ai
Date: 2026-10-18T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Spike across inference routes — urgent

Naomi,

We started seeing serious performance regressions at ~08:45 PT this morning. Latency across our chat.generate calls jumped from ~120ms p50 to ~450ms p50, error rate climbed to ~6.8% on 5xx responses, and throughput recovered only to ~40% of our baseline despite normal traffic. This is affecting our checkout assistance flow and content moderation — we're getting customer complaints.

Can you confirm this is on Redwood's side? We need an ETA and an interim mitigation we can present to our execs.

Thanks,
Alex
VP Product, Firefly.ai
(Attachment: firefly-latency-dashboard-20261018.png)

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-18T09:16:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Spike across inference routes — urgent

Folks — forwarding firefly's report. High urgency; they are a strategic mid-market expansion and this is bleeding into procurement and their CFO. Please treat as command-lane escalation.

Immediate asks:
- Can infra confirm whether this is correlated with the 04:00 deployment (kernel selector change) or a hardware scheduling anomaly?
- SRE: Can we execute emergency routing to fallback model variant (smaller quantized) and open burst capacity?
- Customer comms: I will draft an executive note in 20 minutes; Jordan — please stand by for a bridge invite if we need a direct exec-to-exec.

Attachments: support-logs-firefly-20261018.zip (logs from 07:30–09:10)

Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | naomi_feldman@redwood.ai | +1-415-555-0198

---- Original message attached below ----

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-18T09:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Spike across inference routes — urgent

Naomi — initial triage: 1) No scheduled infra maintenance at 04:00; the 04:00 kernel selector rollout completed but gated to 5% of traffic. 2) Telemetry shows a rapid growth in KV cache eviction rates starting 08:40 which can cause throughput collapse for long-tail sessions. 3) We have elevated GPU queue latency on the west-coast Dedicated pool (pool-d-wc-3).

Immediate actions I'm authorizing now:
- Ben: flip routing policy to prioritize p99 latency SLO routes and activate fallback to model:v2-quant-small for non-critical routes (10 min).
- SRE: spin an emergency burst node in us-west and attach to pool-d-wc-3 (ETA 12 min).
- Ops: throttle tenant-level concurrency for Firefly to limit head-of-line blocking (temp, will coordinate with Naomi).

I'll run a concise exec summary at :35 and join the bridge.

Karthik Iyer
VP Engineering — Serving & Reliability
Redwood Inference

>

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-18T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Re: Fwd: Spike across inference routes — urgent

Confirming actions taken and near-term observations:
- Routing: fallback to model:v2-quant-small is live for non-critical routes. Chat.generate for checkout path remains pinned to primary but with reduced concurrency limit.
- Burst node: us-west-burst-07 spun and attached; initial token throughput increased ~30%.
- Logs: KV cache eviction correlated with a particular session pattern (long conversational threads + repeated streaming reconnects). We have a mitigation patch to adjust cache retention policy for affected tenants queued for hot deploy (5–10 min).

Customer comms draft below — Naomi, can you share with Alex and Dana once I confirm the patch is live? I recommend we lead with what we did, the expected ETA for full recovery (2 hrs worst case) and offering 10% credit for impacted usage in the week.

— Draft external update —
Subject: Interim update — Firefly performance incident (Oct 18)

Alex / Dana,

Wanted to update you quickly on steps we've taken:
- Enabled emergency fallback routing to a compatible quantized model for non-critical routes to restore throughput.
- Added burst capacity in us-west and adjusted concurrency limits to reduce head-of-line blocking.
- Rolling a targeted cache-retention fix to reduce eviction pressure (deploying now).

We expect progressive recovery over the next 30–90 minutes and continued stabilization within 2 hours. We'll follow with a full RCA and a MAP for preventing recurrence.

Regards,
Naomi (on behalf of Redwood Inference)

(Attachment: mutual-action-plan-firefly-20261018.xlsx)

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@firefly.ai>, Dana Liu <dana.liu@firefly.ai>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-18T09:52:00-07:00
Subject: Interim update — Firefly performance incident (Oct 18)

Alex / Dana —

Quick update from the command lane:
- What we saw: increased p50/p95 latency and elevated 5xx error rate beginning ~08:40 PT; impacted chat.generate and moderation routes.
- What we did: activated emergency fallback to a compatible quantized model for non-critical routes; added a burst node in us-west; throttled tenant concurrency to reduce queuing; deploying cache-retention fix now.
- Current status: throughput up ~60% from worst-case, error rate down to ~1.9% and trending down. Some higher-latency sessions remain; full stabilization expected within 2 hours.

We will provide a post-incident RCA and MAP within 48 hours and propose a bilateral runbook change to pin checkout-critical routes to a prioritized pool. As a gesture for the impact, we will apply a one-time credit of 10% on impacted usage for the week — Jordan will connect with procurement on paperwork.

Please let me know if you want an exec bridge. We can stand that up in 15 minutes (Karthik & Ben on the bridge).

Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: firefly-latency-dashboard-20261018.png)

From: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@firefly.ai>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: dana.liu@firefly.ai, procurement@firefly.ai
Date: 2026-10-19T17:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Interim update — Firefly performance incident (Oct 18)

Naomi — thank you for the clear, timely updates and for the credit offer. The burst + cache fix did the trick; our telemetry shows normalized latency by 16:15 PT and only a few sporadic 5xx traces.

We appreciate the quick action and the post-incident MAP. Dana asked me to confirm the MAP and the proposed runbook change (pin checkout-critical routes) — procurement will expect a short SOW for guaranteed capacity and a note on any SLA adjustments.

I'll expect the RCA and MAP doc; please route the DocuSign and SOW to procurement@firefly.ai and I'll loop Dana.

Best,
Alex
(Attachment: support-logs-firefly-20261018.zip)
